entities.name: PMID:10737368
observations: Life Sciences 2000 study used FDG-PET to compare acute alcohol effects in active cocaine abusers and non-cocaine-using controls.
Participants: 9 active cocaine abusers and 10 controls; oral alcohol dose was 0.75 g/kg and plasma alcohol levels were equivalent.

entities.name: Cocaine abuse
observations: Active cocaine abusers showed a smaller alcohol-induced reduction in brain glucose metabolism than controls.

entities.name: Alcohol
observations: Acute oral alcohol at 0.75 g/kg decreased whole-brain glucose metabolism in both groups, with a smaller decrease in cocaine abusers.
Whole-brain decrease was 17±10% in cocaine abusers versus 26±6% in controls despite equivalent plasma alcohol levels.

entities.name: Limbic regions
observations: Regional FDG-PET analyses reported blunted alcohol-induced responses in limbic regions, as well as cingulate gyrus, medial frontal cortex, and orbitofrontal cortex; individual amygdala or hippocampal subregions were not specified in the abstract.

entities.name: Blunted alcohol response
observations: In a small human FDG-PET study, acute alcohol produced a significantly smaller reduction in glucose metabolism in active cocaine abusers than controls, including limbic regions.
